newsitem.title: SWEDEN: SWEDISH SHARES END LOWER AS ERICSSON, ASTRA SLIDE.
newsitem.headline: SWEDISH SHARES END LOWER AS ERICSSON, ASTRA SLIDE.

text.p: Swedish share prices ended lower on Wednesday despite a slight recovery after U.S. July PPI and retail sales data came in more moderately than expected.
The general index slid 1.83 percent to 3,207.13 after heavy turnover totalling 6.17 billion crowns.
Profit-takers brought down telecoms group Ericsson and the share tumbled eight crowns to 356.
Drug company Astra fell 7.5 crowns to 134.5.
Analysts cut forecasts for 1997 earnings of Astra by about 440 million crowns since the group reported a weaker than expected result for the first half, a Reuter poll showed.

Forestry company SCA fell 3.5 crowns to 192.5 after posting a higher than expected profit for the first half of 1997, a 35 percent rise in profit after financial items of 2.25 billion crowns. The sector index edged down 0.37 percent.
The report added weight to expectations of the sector enjoying the rest of the year but fears for 1998 remained. Brokers said there was some profittaking in the sector.
S-E-Banken raised its recommendation on AssiDoman to a 'buy' from 'outperform'. It rose 4.5 crowns to 244.5.
The banking sector continued to fall, losing 3.51 percent, after S-E-Banken reported a disappointing first six months a day earlier. S-E-Banken fell six crowns to 90.
Security company Securitas fell six crowns to 215 after it posted a largely flat profit for the first six months of 1997 of 230 million crowns against 228 million a year ago.
"The result was lower than expectations and the company also lowered its growth forecast to 10-15 percent having previously forecast longterm growth of 20 percent," an analyst said.
Scandinavian airline SAS closed 11 crowns higher at 124 after posting a six-percent dip in profits for the first six months of the year at 1.11 billion crowns.
